text: Everyone judges a catcher by how fast he throws to second.
spoken: Everyone judges a catcher by how fast he throws to second.

text: But that's only half the story.

text: Because before the catcher can even make a throw, the pitcher has to deliver the ball.
spoken: Because before the catcher can even make a throw, the pitcher has to deliver the ball.

text: Let's say the pitcher takes 1.4 seconds to deliver, and the catcher has a 1.9-second pop time.
spoken: Let's say the pitcher takes one point four seconds to deliver, and the catcher has a one point nine second pop time.

text: That's 3.3 seconds before accounting for the runner's jump and the tag.

text: Now compare that with a pitcher who delivers in 1.2 seconds.

text: That's two-tenths of a second less time for the runner to advance.
spoken: That's two-tenths of a second less time for the runner to advance.

text: And that's why stopping a stolen base isn't just a catching problem.
spoken: And that's why stopping a stolen base isn't just a catching problem.

text: It's a race between the pitcher's delivery, the catcher's throw, and the runner's jump.

text: So next time a runner steals second, don't just blame the catcher.
